narrative.overview:
MOS-GIS is a dark-mode precision instrument. Its surfaces are the control room of a research observatory: deep black-blue voids, instrument panels that reveal data on demand, and a single signal-green acquisition color that marks what is live, active, and reachable. Nothing glows for decoration. Every lit element has a reason.

The aesthetic is neither developer-tool austere nor enterprise-platform heavy. It is a calm, public-facing scientific interface. Density is moderate. Typography is clear and purposeful. The service grid is the primary interaction surface — six cards, each a gateway.

This system explicitly rejects heavy enterprise GIS aesthetics: crowded navigation, tiny muted text, navy-on-gray palettes. It equally rejects flashy SaaS conventions: no hero metrics, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism.
keyCharacteristics: Dark surfaces with tonal depth (background → surface → surface-hover), no shadows
One signal accent (Acquisition Green) used sparingly for active states and primary actions
Service-specific colors scoped to badges only — never bled into layout
System font stack — legible and neutral, letting data carry weight
French primary voice, calm and direct, no marketing language

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Acquisition Green (#3ecf8e) is the only color that communicates interactivity or live status outside of service badges. If a new interactive element appears on the page, its active/live state uses this color. No other color takes that role.

rules.name: The Scoped Badge Rule
rules.body: Service accent colors (Cartesian Blue, Thermal Amber, Geodesic Violet, Process Emerald, Interface Pink) are badge-only. They do not migrate to headings, borders, backgrounds, buttons, or any element outside a card badge or card icon context.

rules.name: The Single-Family Rule
rules.body: No second typeface is introduced. Not for headings, not for decorative purposes, not for personality. The weight and size hierarchy is the typography.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow on cards, buttons, or containers at rest or on hover. If a floating element appears, it uses a single subtle shadow (0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.5)) against the dark background. This is the only permitted shadow, and only for truly floating elements.

dos: Do use Acquisition Green (#3ecf8e) for primary buttons, active status indicators, wordmark accents, and focus rings. Nothing else.
Do keep service accent colors inside card badges and icon backgrounds only.
Do convey depth through tonal surface shifts (bg → surface → surface-hover). No shadows on cards or containers at rest.
Do keep body text at #e8eaf0 on dark surfaces — never drop to #8b92a8 for running descriptions.
Do use the system font stack. No web fonts unless a specific typographic need is confirmed.
Do limit uppercase to labels of 4 words or fewer.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: every transition has a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) override.
Do write UI copy in French first, direct and brief — no tech buzzwords in visible labels.
donts: Don't use dense enterprise GIS aesthetics: crowded navigation, tiny muted body text, navy-on-gray color palettes.
Don't introduce SaaS dashboard conventions: no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism cards, no background-clip gradient headings.
Don't use box-shadow on cards or buttons. The flat tonal system is intentional.
Don't bleed service accent colors outside their card.
Don't use Void Text (#555d78) for body content.
Don't use border-left or border-right as a colored accent stripe on cards or callouts.
